attempts.summary: Set up self-managed HTTPS certificate rotation on node1: nginx serves TLS on port 8443 using a certificate issued by a local CA (/etc/pki/rotating-cert). A systemd oneshot service (rotate-node1-cert.service) + timer (rotate-node1-cert.timer, hourly checks) automatically reissues the leaf certificate before it expires (renews when <2 days remain of a 7-day validity window) and gracefully reloads nginx (`nginx -s reload`) so the new certificate is picked up with zero dropped requests. Live rotation was demonstrated end-to-end under compressed timing (180s cert life / 120s renewal threshold / 30s timer) with a continuous curl probe: certificate serial changed automatically from ...CA3D to ...CA3E while HTTP 200 responses continued uninterrupted, then production-realistic timing was restored. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline (910dc564...), issued a native `reboot` via systemd-run (ack returned before disconnection), polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (→79f4bd20...) proving an actual restart, and verified nginx + the rotation timer came back active/enabled with the listener up, the cert intact and valid, and live HTTPS requests succeeding post-reboot.
